passages.text: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.
passages.sermon:
The high priest was named Ananias.
Ananias came down after five days.
He brought some elders with him.
He also brought a lawyer named Tertullus.
Ananias, the elders, and Tertullus went to the governor.
They presented their case against Paul to the governor.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ πέντε ἡμέρας κατέβη ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς Ἁνανίας μετὰ πρεσβυτέρων τινῶν καὶ ῥήτορος Τερτύλλου τινός οἵτινες ἐνεφάνισαν τῷ ἡγεμόνι κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου

passages.text: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the governor Felix.
Tertullus was a lawyer.
Tertullus began to accuse Paul.
Tertullus spoke to Felix.
Tertullus said, “Felix, you have given us much peace.
You have brought order to our nation.
You have done this by your careful leadership.”
passages.original: Κληθέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤρξατο κατηγορεῖν ὁ Τέρτυλλος λέγων Πολλῆς εἰρήνης τυγχάνοντες διὰ σοῦ καὶ διορθωμάτων γινομένων τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ διὰ τῆς σῆς προνοίας

passages.text: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.
passages.sermon:
Felix was the governor.
Felix held a high and respected position.
Tertullus spoke to Felix.
Tertullus called Felix “most excellent.”
Tertullus and those with him showed respect to Felix.
They said they were grateful to Felix.
They said they acknowledged Felix’s actions.
They said they did this in every way.
They said they did this everywhere.
They said they did this with all gratitude.
passages.original: πάντῃ τε καὶ πανταχοῦ ἀποδεχόμεθα κράτιστε Φῆλιξ μετὰ πάσης εὐχαριστίας

passages.text: But in order not to burden you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.
passages.sermon:
Tertullus spoke to Felix, the Roman governor.
\r\nTertullus wanted to show respect to Felix.
\r\nTertullus did not want to trouble Felix with a long speech.
\r\nTertullus asked Felix to listen for only a short time.
\r\nTertullus appealed to Felix’s kindness and fairness.
passages.original: ἵνα δὲ μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖόν σε ἐνκόπτω παρακαλῶ ἀκοῦσαί σε ἡμῶν συντόμως τῇ σῇ ἐπιεικείᾳ

passages.text: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes, and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
passages.sermon:
We have found this man to be a troublemaker.
He causes problems among the Jews everywhere in the world.
He leads the group called the Nazarenes.
He tried to make the temple unclean.
We seized him.
passages.original: Εὑρόντες γὰρ τὸν ἄνδρα τοῦτον λοιμὸν καὶ κινοῦντα στάσεις πᾶσιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην πρωτοστάτην τε τῆς τῶν Ναζωραίων αἱρέσεως ὃς καὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐπείρασεν βεβηλῶσαι ὃν καὶ ἐκρατήσαμεν

passages.text: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”
passages.sermon:
You are the governor.
\r\nYou can examine this man yourself.
\r\nYou can question him about all these matters.
\r\nYou will be able to learn the truth about everything we accuse him of.
passages.original: παρ’ οὗ δυνήσῃ αὐτὸς ἀνακρίνας περὶ πάντων τούτων ἐπιγνῶναι ὧν ἡμεῖς κατηγοροῦμεν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true.
passages.sermon: The Jews agreed with the accusations.\r\nThey said the charges were true.
passages.original: Συνεπέθεντο δὲ καὶ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι φάσκοντες ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχειν

passages.text: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the governor.
The governor gave Paul permission to speak.
Paul began to answer.
Paul knew the governor had judged this nation for many years.
Paul spoke with confidence.
Paul was ready to defend himself.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη τε ὁ Παῦλος νεύσαντος αὐτῷ τοῦ ἡγεμόνος λέγειν Ἐκ πολλῶν ἐτῶν ὄντα σε κριτὴν τῷ ἔθνει τούτῳ ἐπιστάμενος εὐθύμως τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἀπολογοῦμαι

passages.text: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the governor.
The governor had authority to judge.
Paul said the governor could check the facts.
Paul said he went up to Jerusalem.
Paul said this happened no more than twelve days ago.
Paul went to Jerusalem to worship.
passages.original: δυναμένου σου ἐπιγνῶναι ὅτι οὐ πλείους εἰσίν μοι ἡμέραι δώδεκα ἀφ’ ἧς ἀνέβην προσκυνήσων εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ

passages.text: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the governor.
Paul spoke about his actions in Jerusalem.
Paul said his accusers did not find him arguing with anyone in the temple.
Paul said his accusers did not find him stirring up a crowd in the temple.
Paul said his accusers did not find him causing trouble in the synagogues.
Paul said his accusers did not find him causing trouble anywhere in the city.
passages.original: καὶ οὔτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ εὗρόν με πρός τινα διαλεγόμενον ἢ ἐπίστασιν ποιοῦντα ὄχλου οὔτε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς οὔτε κατὰ τὴν πόλιν

passages.text: Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.
passages.sermon: My accusers cannot prove their charges against me.\r\nThey cannot show you any evidence for what they now accuse me of.
passages.original: οὐδὲ παραστῆσαι δύνανταί σοι περὶ ὧν νυνὶ κατηγοροῦσίν μου

passages.text: I do confess to you, however, that I worship the God of our fathers according to the Way, which they call a sect. I believe everything that is laid down by the Law and written in the Prophets, and I have the same hope in God that they themselves cherish, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the governor.
Paul is a follower of Jesus.
Paul worships the God of his ancestors.
Paul follows the Way.
The Way is what his accusers call a sect.
Paul believes everything in the Law.
Paul believes everything written in the Prophets.
Paul has hope in God.
Paul’s hope is the same as his accusers’ hope.
Paul believes there will be a resurrection.
God will raise both the righteous and the wicked.
passages.original: Ὁμολογῶ δὲ τοῦτό σοι ὅτι κατὰ τὴν Ὁδὸν ἣν λέγουσιν αἵρεσιν οὕτως λατρεύω τῷ πατρῴῳ Θεῷ πιστεύων πᾶσι τοῖς κατὰ τὸν νόμον καὶ τοῖς ἐν τοῖς προφήταις γεγραμμένοις ἐλπίδα ἔχων εἰς τὸν Θεόν ἣν καὶ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι προσδέχονται ἀνάστασιν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι δικαίων τε καὶ ἀδίκων

passages.text: In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
\r\nPaul believes in the resurrection of the dead.
\r\nPaul hopes in God.
\r\nBecause of this hope, Paul acts in a certain way.
\r\nPaul always tries to keep a clear conscience.
\r\nPaul wants a clear conscience before God.
\r\nPaul wants a clear conscience before people.
\r\nPaul works to do this at all times.
passages.original: ἐν τούτῳ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀσκῶ ἀπρόσκοπον συνείδησιν ἔχειν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους διὰ παντός

passages.text: After several years, then, I returned to Jerusalem to bring alms to my people and to present offerings.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking.
Paul is a follower of Jesus.
Paul returned to Jerusalem after several years.
Paul came to bring alms to his people.
Paul also came to present offerings.
passages.original: Δι’ ἐτῶν δὲ πλειόνων ἐλεημοσύνας ποιήσων εἰς τὸ ἔθνος μου παρεγενόμην καὶ προσφοράς

passages.text: At the time they found me in the temple, I was ceremonially clean and was not inciting a crowd or an uproar. But there are some Jews from the province of Asia who ought to appear before you and bring charges, if they have anything against me.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood in the temple.
Paul was ceremonially clean.
Paul did not have a crowd with him.
Paul did not cause any uproar.
Some Jews came from the province of Asia.
These Jews should be here before you.
They should bring charges if they have anything against Paul.
passages.original: ἐν αἷς εὗρόν με ἡγνισμένον ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ οὐ μετὰ ὄχλου οὐδὲ μετὰ θορύβου τινὲς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἀσίας Ἰουδαῖοι οὓς ἔδει ἐπὶ σοῦ παρεῖναι καὶ κατηγορεῖν εἴ τι ἔχοιεν πρὸς ἐμέ

passages.text: Otherwise, let these men state for themselves any crime they found in me when I stood before the Sanhedrin, unless it was this one thing I called out as I stood in their presence: ‘It is concerning the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial before you today.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before the Sanhedrin.
Paul was on trial.
Paul spoke to the men accusing him.
Paul said, "Let these men say what crime they found in me."
Paul said, "They should tell you if I did anything wrong."
Paul said, "There is only one thing I called out while I stood among them."
Paul said, "I called out, 'I am on trial before you today because of the resurrection of the dead.'"
Paul made it clear that the resurrection of the dead was the reason for his trial.
passages.original: ἢ αὐτοὶ οὗτοι εἰπάτωσαν τί εὗρον ἀδίκημα στάντος μου ἐπὶ τοῦ συνεδρίου ἢ περὶ μιᾶς ταύτης φωνῆς ἧς ἐκέκραξα ἐν αὐτοῖς ἑστὼς ὅτι Περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν ἐγὼ κρίνομαι σήμερον ἐφ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: Then Felix, who was well informed about the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”
passages.sermon:
Felix was the Roman governor.
Felix knew much about the Way.
The Way was the early Christian movement.
Felix stopped the hearing.
Felix said, “When Lysias the commander comes, I will decide your case.”
passages.original: Ἀνεβάλετο δὲ αὐτοὺς ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀκριβέστερον εἰδὼς τὰ περὶ τῆς Ὁδοῦ εἴπας Ὅταν Λυσίας ὁ χιλίαρχος καταβῇ διαγνώσομαι τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς

passages.text: He ordered the centurion to keep Paul under guard, but to allow him some freedom and permit his friends to minister to his needs.
passages.sermon:
Felix was the Roman governor.
Felix gave an order to the centurion.
Felix told the centurion to keep Paul under guard.
Felix also told the centurion to give Paul some freedom.
Felix allowed Paul’s friends to visit him.
Felix permitted Paul’s friends to take care of his needs.
passages.original: διαταξάμενος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἔχειν τε ἄνεσιν καὶ μηδένα κωλύειν τῶν ἰδίων αὐτοῦ ὑπηρετεῖν αὐτῷ

passages.text: After several days, Felix returned with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess. He sent for Paul and listened to him speak about faith in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Felix was the Roman governor.
Drusilla was his wife.
Drusilla was Jewish.
After several days, Felix returned.
Felix came with Drusilla.
Felix sent for Paul.
Paul came to Felix and Drusilla.
Felix listened to Paul.
Paul spoke about faith in Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ ἡμέρας τινὰς παραγενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ σὺν Δρουσίλλῃ τῇ ἰδίᾳ γυναικὶ οὔσῃ Ἰουδαίᾳ μετεπέμψατο τὸν Παῦλον καὶ ἤκουσεν αὐτοῦ περὶ τῆς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν πίστεως

passages.text: As Paul expounded on righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became frightened and said, “You may go for now. When I find the time, I will call for you.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke about righteousness.
Paul spoke about self-control.
Paul spoke about the coming judgment.
Felix listened to Paul.
Felix became afraid.
Felix said, “You may go for now.”
Felix said, “When I find the time, I will call for you.”
passages.original: διαλεγομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περὶ δικαιοσύνης καὶ ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ κρίματος τοῦ μέλλοντος ἔμφοβος γενόμενος ὁ Φῆλιξ ἀπεκρίθη Τὸ νῦν ἔχον πορεύου καιρὸν δὲ μεταλαβὼν μετακαλέσομαί σε

passages.text: At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him a bribe. So he sent for Paul frequently and talked with him.
passages.sermon:
Felix was the Roman governor.
Felix hoped Paul would give him money.
Felix wanted a bribe from Paul.
Felix sent for Paul often.
Felix talked with Paul many times.
passages.original: ἅμα καὶ ἐλπίζων ὅτι χρήματα δοθήσεται αὐτῷ ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου διὸ καὶ πυκνότερον αὐτὸν μεταπεμπόμενος ὡμίλει αὐτῷ

passages.text: After two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And wishing to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in prison.
passages.sermon:
Felix was the Roman governor.
Two years passed.
Porcius Festus replaced Felix as governor.
Felix wanted to please the Jews.
Felix left Paul in prison.
passages.original: Διετίας δὲ πληρωθείσης ἔλαβεν διάδοχον ὁ Φῆλιξ Πόρκιον Φῆστον θέλων τε χάριτα καταθέσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὁ Φῆλιξ κατέλιπε τὸν Παῦλον δεδεμένον
